He attended the Institute of Art, Design and Fashion in Turin, where he was the only boy in an all-female school. At 17 he began collaborating with newspapers and magazines, drawing sketches from high fashion shows, first from Rome and then from Paris. Here he meets Coco Chanel, his icon and muse.
ad0734c09534bf1a4b64f4cd8a3bb19d65b70095: His talent did not go unnoticed and he was soon hired by important Italian fashion houses, such as Krizia, Cadette and Trell. In the same year he presented the Anagrafe collection, composed of eight long pink brides and eight short black widows.
603f73cd1d075bd4d7ee21137f1f4a0ff508e318: Walter Albini is the first to understand the potential of ready-to-wear, that is, ready-to-wear, accessible and quality fashion. To realize his vision, he decides to collaborate with five fashion houses specialized in product types, coordinated according to a unified style project. d88c2adfac003576aa9e776cae754f00176be0b1: Albini chose to present his creations in Milan and not in Florence, then the capital of Italian fashion. In the same year he opened the showroom in via Pietro Cossa in Milan and moved to Venice, where he organized a memorable fashion show at the Florian café.

b9c6f33a1843c040bb41efb6aa455c2e7bc40556: Air Jordans are a line of sports shoes created in 1984 by Nike for basketball champion Michael Jordan, considered one of the best players of all time. The name derives from his athletic skills and his aerial game, which made him famous throughout the world. Air Jordans are not just simple basketball shoes, but have become a cultural phenomenon, a symbol of style and success, an object of desire for millions of fans and collectors. In this article we tell you the history, characteristics and curiosities of these legendary sneakers.
9efce507ca575e96d8447d770ebcf7230efd116f: The history of Air Jordan begins in 1984, when Nike, an American sports clothing and accessories company, decided to create a brand dedicated to Michael Jordan, a young and talented Chicago Bulls player who had just entered the NBA. Jordan was looking for a sponsor who could enhance his image and personality on the pitch. Initially, his dream was to collaborate with Adidas, but it was his mother, Deloris, who convinced him to go to the meeting with Nike. The company's offer was too tempting to refuse: $250,000 a year for five years, plus a percentage of shoe sales. Furthermore, Nike guaranteed him maximum creative freedom and the possibility of having an exclusive line in his name.
ac8fb4e574cb554f482e1dd5b44830262e11543a: The Air Jordan brand was coined by Jordan's agent, David Falk, who was inspired by the nickname "Air" that the player had received for his spectacular dunks. The logo chosen was the Jumpman, which is the stylized silhouette of Jordan jumping with his legs apart and the ball in his hand. The first shoe model was designed by Peter Moore and was called Air Jordan I. It featured a high cut, a leather upper on which the large swoosh (the Nike logo) stood out and another logo dedicated to the Jordan line consisting of a winged ball and the word "Air Jordan" located near the neck of the shoe. As for the colors, the shoes were predominantly black and red, in homage to the Chicago Bulls.
94aae848bca605ca66c26ec5ca6fb2fdcb6a8d99: [0][1]The controversies and success of the Air Jordan[3][4]
f2db8c759b3181da144c6b879cf1d78c4f72673f: The Air Jordan I made their official debut on the market in March 1985, but even before that they had attracted a lot of interest and even some controversy. In fact, Michael Jordan had worn them during some games of the 1984-1985 season, violating the NBA rules which required players to wear white shoes or shoes with uniform colors to those of the uniform. For this reason, the league fined Jordan $5,000 every time he wore his "banned" shoes. However, Nike decided to pay the fines for him and used the opportunity to create a brilliant advertising campaign. The commercial featured images of the shoes with a voiceover saying, "On October 15, the NBA launched a revolution. It banned these shoes from the game. Luckily, the NBA can't stop you from wearing them." The message was clear: Air Jordans were the most rebellious, innovative and desirable shoes of the moment.
b3b77df4b3cb9d857a5663d59f3b9711f600ed36: The strategy worked perfectly: the Air Jordan I sold 70 million dollars in the first two months and became a mass phenomenon. Jordan, for his part, confirmed his skills on the field, winning the Rookie of the Year award, participating in the All-Star Game and averaging 28.2 points per game. Nike therefore decided to continue the collaboration with the player and create a new model every year, inspired by his personality, his passions and his performances. Thus was born the series of 23 basketball shoes that made the history of Air Jordan, from 1985 to 2009. Each model had unique technical and stylistic characteristics, which made it different from the others and adapted it to the needs and tastes of Jordan and his fans.
6242727c6b4e3b91c4277a028908eb869ea2edd8: Air Jordans were created to be the most cutting-edge basketball shoes on the market, both in terms of technique and design. For this reason, Nike brought in some of the best designers and engineers in the industry, such as Peter Moore, Tinker Hatfield, Bruce Kilgore, Wilson Smith III and others. Each model had peculiarities that distinguished it from the others and made it recognizable at a glance. Here are some of the most famous:
d932971a5b9f8902e981cb165f864599a9b4b57f: The Air Jordan II was the first basketball shoe to have a suede upper and not have the Nike logo. They were also the first to be produced in Italy, to give a touch of elegance and quality.
12ec34ad9085ee2aa7dc0ccb0a3a9934da987fba: The Air Jordan III was the first to introduce the Jumpman logo in place of the winged football and to incorporate a visible bladder in the heel to improve cushioning. They were also the first to feature the famous "elephant print" motif on the toe and heel.
c02b8aa11eb7fcb6463fa4f23c5450e511f19e44: The Air Jordan IV were the first to have holes on the upper to facilitate breathability and lacing. They were also the first to be sold on the international market and to be worn by Michael Jordan in the film "Space Jam".
525fb59af6f9c2afd4ba05a86be3255a2770605b: The Air Jordan V were the first to not have the Nike logo on the outside of the shoe, but only on the tongue and sole. They were also the first to have a translucent sole that glowed in the dark and reflective stripes on the heel.
e15daf77a4e15d39c429ddb3d4ef7b80753431e6: The Air Jordan VI was the first to have a hole in the heel to facilitate the fit and a padded tongue to protect the Achilles tendon. They were also the first to have two different colors for the right foot and the left foot.
471f6c9f66d9e401a850e8b18492a65bc4c1dac0: The Air Jordan VII was the first to have the Nike logo neither on the side nor on the sole of the shoe, but only the Jumpman on the heel and tongue. They were also the first to have graphics inspired by African art on the upper.
018e9ad27c0a7fe74a516f86b232d1abfb52f95c: The Air Jordan VIII was the first to have crossed straps on the upper for greater stability and a tongue with a flying carpet design. They were also the first to have a sole with a colorful geometric design.
fd0879f483464f89c07bec829e1e3c90053bae73: The Air Jordan IXs were the first not to be worn by Michael Jordan in an NBA game, but only during his short baseball career. They were also the first to have writing in different languages ​​on the sole to represent the global spirit of the player.
d3d9a5120b712f56ccda8ecb88844523f7f69761: The Air Jordan X was the first to celebrate Michael Jordan's accomplishments with a list of his accomplishments on the outsole. They were also the first to have the metal Jumpman logo on the side of the shoe.
ebdea23cb87a9842cb0ec49172d4b4b6521eb8a1: The Air Jordan XI was the first to use Nike's patented material called "patent leather"
ca9b338ed676ee0d27b1650585519f1fbcee1d9c: The Air Jordan XII was the first to use Zoom Air technology for greater responsiveness and comfort. They were also the first to be inspired by a non-sporting object, namely the flag of Japan.
3f55c631a8f1a653a07624067616a0cc2fe0b18b: The Air Jordan XIII was the first to feature a cat-paw outsole, a nod to Jordan's "Black Cat" nickname. They were also the first to incorporate a hologram on the heel that simulated the eye of a feline.
366bf6668a6c35b0fb4d4d8d033b886e14fa302c: The Air Jordan XIV were the first to be influenced by the world of racing cars, in particular by the Ferrari 550 Maranello. They were also the last to be worn by Jordan with the Chicago Bulls in 1998.

71efffdc9cf0b76873bf732746b5baf35df5c39f: The Air Jordan XVI was the first to feature a removable upper that transformed the shoe from a high-top to a low-top. They were also the first to have a transparent sole with the Jumpman logo embossed.
27a12ceec3badea6967beece94da8cbe0e753f69: The Air Jordan XVII was the first to exceed $200 in price and to be sold in a metal briefcase. They were also the first to have a sole with a musical design that referenced Jordan's passion for jazz.
5f0d50c4495b7f0f4eb66417ee171525cd0da3a5: The Air Jordan XVIII was the first to be inspired by classic Italian shoes, with a clean toe box and hidden tongue. They were also the last ones to be worn by Jordan in the NBA in 2003.

0be7dc2e7281ce2e0cec982f013320eb35825aa5: Italy is world famous for its art, its culture and its fashion. 801d66a3e2e18e59682997fd9a2911d8b3239a3f: Gianfranco Ferrè (Legnano, 1944 – Milan, 2007) was one of the most famous and appreciated Italian stylists in the world. Graduated in architecture, he began his career in 1970, launching collections for women, men and children, as well as accessories and perfumes. His style was characterized by great attention to the shape, structure and details of the garments, which earned him the nickname "the architect of fashion". Among his most important successes are the artistic direction of the Dior fashion house from 1989 to 1996 and the creation of the GF Ferrè brand in 1999.
bba566667c30fdc7e9145c7d58652ea91e96d3a4: Elsa Schiaparelli (Rome, 1890 – Paris, 1973) was one of the first and most original Italian stylists in history. Having moved to Paris in the 1920s, she began collaborating with surrealist artists such as Salvador Dalí and Jean Cocteau, transferring their vision to the world of fashion. His creations were bold, extravagant and ironic, such as the famous hat in the shape of an upside-down shoe, the dress with a large lobster printed on the skirt or the tattered and torn evening dress. She also invented the trouser skirt and the shocking pink colour, becoming an icon of style and creative freedom.
981f6a07902332f0f93bacff192b6ea569b30b70: Alberta Ferretti (Cattolica, 1950) is one of the most elegant and refined Italian stylists on the contemporary scene. She founded her company in 1974 and debuted on the Milanese catwalks in 1981. Her style is romantic, feminine and sophisticated, based on the use of fine fabrics, delicate embroidery and pastel colours. Among his most famous collections, we remember the one dedicated to Disney princesses in 2016 and the one inspired by nature in 2019. He also created the Philosophy brand in 1984 and the Aeffe brand in 1986.
2ad6a716618525daf3680590316c396bba85566a: Gianni Versace (Reggio Calabria, 1946 – Miami Beach, 1997) was one of the most influential and beloved Italian designers in history. He founded his maison in 1978 in Milan and conquered the world with his glamorous, sensual and provocative collections, which mixed elements of pop culture, art and Greek mythology. Among its most iconic pieces, we remember the safety dress worn by Elizabeth Hurley in 1994, the jungle dress worn by Jennifer Lopez in 2000 and the gold dress worn by Naomi Campbell in 1998. After her tragic death, which occurred at the hands of a serial killer, her company was carried on by her brothers Donatella and Santo.
48fd7656e0575a977f7eeb9d5d8320dba22b7292: Miuccia Prada (Milan, 1949) is one of the most innovative and influential Italian designers in contemporary fashion. He inherited the family business, founded in 1913 by Mario Prada, in 1978 and transformed it into a luxury empire, launching collections of clothing, accessories, perfumes and eyewear. His style is eclectic, intellectual and non-conformist, capable of anticipating trends and creating new aesthetic codes. Among his most famous inventions are silk-effect nylon, the triangular logo and the Miu Miu line, created in 1993. He also founded the Prada Foundation in 1993, dedicated to the promotion of art and culture.
807dd8183997889646f16c41f9b266d8170e79f9: Guccio Gucci (Florence, 1881 – Milan, 1953) was the founder of the Gucci fashion house, one of the most prestigious and famous in the world. 9fffd88761b9f4d0ab6bf80f084cd7702c6a4805: Giorgio Armani (Piacenza, 1934) is one of the most famous and appreciated Italian designers in the world. fa14a96a58ba95a94cc30f2efaa38a50f8c457f1: Giovanni Maria Versace, known as Gianni, was born in Reggio Calabria on 2 December 1946, following the birth of his brother Santo and anticipating that of his sister Donatella. He had his first contacts with the world of fashion as a boy, working in the atelier of his mother Francesca, a professional seamstress. From her he learned the secrets of the trade and developed his passion for art and classical culture. At the age of 14 he attended the Tommaso Campanella classical high school, without completing his studies.
2daf52e9db3e27c5fe5b0c241a29f2eded6dfcfb: In 1972, at the age of twenty-five, he moved to Milan to work as a clothing designer, creating the first collections for Genny, Complice and Callaghan. In 1975 he presented his first collection of leather clothes for Complice. On 28 March 1978 at the Palazzo della Permanente, in Milan, Gianni Versace presented the first women's collection signed with his name. The following year he began a successful collaboration with the American photographer Richard Avedon, who created his advertising campaigns until 1994.
851806b10a9763c856a1ff0e76f43b4c27468ba1: In the 80s and 90s, Gianni Versace achieved international success with his collections that expressed an original and bold vision of fashion. His style is characterized by the use of bright colors, animal prints, metallic elements, leather and silk. Versace is inspired by its homeland, Greek and Roman mythology, baroque, pop art, rock and cinema. His creations are worn by stars such as Madonna, Elton John, Michael Jackson, Lady Diana and many others.
cf7316605a7ffd1644228ce888aa35c335846985: Versace is also the inventor of the top models, the supermodels who become icons of beauty and fame. His muses include Naomi Campbell, Cindy Crawford, Linda Evangelista, Christy Turlington and Claudia Schiffer. One of the most famous images of his career is the one from 1991 in which the five models sing Freedom by George Michael on the catwalk of his show.
ca1339bc91305b094e68f487eba2e73acb358257: Versace is not limited to fashion, but is also dedicated to theatre, ballet and opera. He designed costumes for numerous operas including Josephslegende by Richard Strauss, Don Pasquale by Gaetano Donizetti, Dyonisos by Maurice Béjart and Capriccio by Richard Strauss. b5bef96b394468d835db7dcc17b56c65f9310fbd: On the morning of July 15, 1997, Gianni Versace was killed in front of the gate of his villa in Miami Beach by Andrew Cunanan, a serial killer wanted for four other murders. a3b20dfdb9e59d8f40f672a2983d7e92e3c93b23: [0][1]The life and works of Yves Saint Laurent[3][4]

c855b0e1d0a3daa78de0026e325cb195317dad65: What are Walter Albini's clothing lines?
3340b5d98ff2e2ebbfa7b8e133114dda6a0710f9: Walter Albini marked the birth of Italian ready-to-wear with iconic lines such as “Unimax” and the Anagrafe collection, redefining total style and inspiring generations of designers.
e1e0d99cf71dc21880577639c74cbd4378ad26d9: [0]Walter Albini[2] revolutionized the Italian fashion industry by introducing an innovative approach that combines haute couture and industrial production. Born in 1941 in Busto Arsizio, Albini studied art in Turin and gained international experience in Paris and London, marking his encounter with figures such as Coco Chanel and Karl Lagerfeld. His most relevant intuition was to bring creativity to the factory, guaranteeing quality and stylistic coherence to collections created on a large scale. With the birth of its lines, Albini has overcome the traditional separation between haute couture and ready-to-wear, creating a bridge between luxury and accessibility for a new audience of consumers.
ac121eab69a5fdf3082559d8d112350b1878b755: Walter Albini's path begins in the industrial fabric of Northern Italy, where from a young age he developed particular attention to materials and production processes. After graduating from the Academy of Fine Arts in Turin, he continued his training in Paris, working alongside Coco Chanel, who conveyed the cult of clean lines and timeless elegance. The meeting with Karl Lagerfeld at Courrèges opens up new perspectives on stylistic innovation and the use of technical fabrics. These international experiences forge the theoretical basis that Albini will apply in Italy, positioning himself as a mediator between craftsmanship and industrial production.
f2640b5d011ea241c38e27e2c965bb1eb0b8baeb: [0][1]2. The first collaborations and the approach to ready-to-wear[3][4]
a14ae3bcec0d09d2270516ff4e94fad0b86b7a65: In the late 1960s, Albini began collaborating with rising fashion houses such as Krizia, Cadette, Billy Ballo and Trell, as well as the famous American brand Cole of California. In these contexts he experiments with his first ready-to-wear collections, applying the concept of "functional fashion" which favors wearability, versatility and speed of production. His work with Krizia, in particular, highlights the ability to combine formal research and a commercial approach, anticipating seasonal trends. This consolidation phase leads Albini to define his own aesthetic language based on precise cuts and essential color palettes.
b814db8201f2e58e38a2032d4d3365ecfae97119: In 1970 Walter Albini launched the [1]Unimax[3] project, a production philosophy based on uniformity of cut and color for men and women. The goal was to create basic garments, easily recognizable and usable on multiple occasions, breaking down the barriers between male and female aesthetics. This pioneering experiment demonstrated how a minimal design could find favor with the market without sacrificing sartorial rigor.
84a3a022e37a26c5c2d893ff7a423e9a6ca79a54: The Unimax proposal included color palettes reduced to primary nuances, easy-to-work fabrics and standardized models. Thanks to factory production, these garments were accessible in terms of price and available on a large scale, bringing Italian ready-to-wear to an international level. The success of Unimax marked a turning point in the industry, inspiring other designers to experiment with similar formulas.
70dda7aaa48a3ce98849407fab47e10cd04e6058: The [1]Anagrafe[3] collection, also presented in 1970, was a true conceptual manifesto. Albini created eight brides dressed in powder pink and eight widows in black, creating a dramatic contrast between emotional sunrises and sunsets. Each look, accompanied by minimalist accessories, evoked stories of multiple identities and social masks.
21def47a6e3ae720cb12ba6eabef604f8d55dbfe: Anagrafe aimed to spark reflections on the role of women in contemporary society, using fashion as a narrative medium. The light fabrics and geometric cuts gave an air of modernity deliberately distant from romantic clichés. The media coverage was strong, with dedicated reports in the main Italian and international fashion magazines.
69b2fa82f71ba183cca62dc7384b586aed788cda: To translate his vision into productive reality, Albini organized five companies specialized in different categories: women's clothing, menswear, knitwear, accessories and footwear. Each company branch maintained operational autonomy, but responded to a single creative direction, guaranteeing consistency of style and quality.
59164b6d7e3fbc174e1d91fc38df3471566ed6fd: This innovative business model allowed the offer to be diversified without losing the brand's identity. Thanks to internal specialization, production times were reduced and the ability to react to market trends increased considerably. The system became a point of reference for other ready-to-wear realities in Italy.
5fe0b3565864a446a5a6e494c5365f2fa5ebd152: In 1973 Albini presented his first personal collection in London, giving life to the eponymous brand [1]Walter Albini[3]. 59f53482378c629f76b7248d6d83ae2f0a4846de: The garments of the first personal line stood out for their essential cuts, sartorial details and fine materials such as virgin wool and textured silk. c877e6ffa52f647cf057908eabf5f6723ce6351c: With the concept of [1]total look[3], Albini no longer limits itself to clothing, but extends its signature to accessories, home textiles and design objects. df838ffa8d9b98dc3948f44a50e24f32cd101d37: The photographic campaigns of those years showed domestic settings and shots of passers-by in urban contexts, highlighting the wearability of the garments and the aesthetic coherence.
